summary: Intermittent TTFB spikes and long-tail streaming latency traced to API Gateway write coalescing
description: Customer reports intermittent increases in time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streaming completions. Spikes occur during short burst traffic windows and manifest as 2–30s delays before the first token is delivered; downstream tokens stream normally once delivery starts. Issue appears correlated with bursts of parallel requests and large auth headers from the customer's side.
impact: ParcelFlow noticed ~8-12% of streaming requests during traffic bursts have TTFB > 5s, with a small fraction hitting > 30s. User-facing video-transcoding microservice that relies on low-latency chat completions experienced retries and degraded UX. No request body loss observed; costs increased due to retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ParcelFlow dedicated tenant in prod-us-east with default routing to dedicated pool
2) Send 200 concurrent streaming chat requests that include a large Authorization header (~6KB JWT rotation token), batching starts at t0
3) Observe initial write between client and API Gateway and monitor TTFB for each request
4) Correlate spikes with APIGW connection metrics and ALB idle send/receive counters
observed_behavior: A subset of requests experience delayed first-write from upstream (APIGW) to load balancer, producing TTFB spikes. After first byte arrives, server streams remain healthy. TCP retransmits and occasional window-clamping seen in packet captures between APIGW and ALB.
expected_behavior: TTFB should be consistent across the burst, with median < 500ms and 95th percentile within SLO for dedicated customers. Streaming should start promptly without multi-second delays.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 13:30 - Support triage: validated customer traffic pattern and reproduced spikes with a synthetic test harness using large auth headers.
2026-03-10 15:05 - SRE collected APIGW internal metrics: write batching/coalescing increases when many small writes happen in short windows (observed 4KB coalescing threshold).

2026-03-10 16:40 - Packet capture between APIGW and ALB shows coalesced writes delayed until a flush event or timer expires, introducing ~10-25ms per connection but accumulates under burst and with TLS handshake/large header processing delays leading to seconds of TTFB in worst cases.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Correlation found between requests carrying rotated JWTs (large headers) and higher incidence of delayed flushes in APIGW.
2026-03-11 11:00 - Reproduced locally with modified APIGW config toggling write_coalesce; disabling coalescing removed TTFB spikes in test harness but increased CPU syscalls on gateway nodes.

2026-03-12 08:20 - Noted similar patterns referenced in SUP-82123 (header-rotation during kv-warmup) but root cause differs: this is APIGW-level coalescing plus header processing latency rather than ALB idle resets alone.
hypotheses: H1: APIGW write coalescing timer is allowing large header processing to block flush, causing grouped flushes and long TTFB under burst loads.
H2: Large Authorization headers trigger extra processing (JWT verification, header parsing) on APIGW that stalls data send until processing completes.
H3: ALB TCP window/clamping combined with coalesced writes amplifies latency, producing long-tail TTFB for a subset of flows.
H4: Client-side retry/backoff patterns are increasing parallelism and head-of-line effects at APIGW sockets.
mitigation: Short term: Rolled out temporary APIGW config change to reduce write coalescing window from 10ms to 1ms for ParcelFlow's tenant, mitigates >90% of reproduced spikes (applied 2026-03-11 14:30).
Workaround: Customer advised to reduce Authorization header size by using shorter-lived tokens with server-side session mapping; provided helper library to exchange large JWT for short opaque token.
Traffic-level: Added a routing rule to send ParcelFlow burst traffic to a warmer pool of gateway instances with higher CPU headroom to reduce header-verification latency.
Monitoring: Added alert rule to detect TTFB 95th > 2s for any dedicated tenant and to surface APIGW write_coalesce metric.
resolution: Mitigation successful in reducing customer-observable spikes. Long-term fix: engineering will implement adaptive coalescing logic that considers per-tenant header-processing latency and falls back to aggressive flush when large headers or JWT verification are detected. Work scheduled: routing service & apigw PRs targeted for 2026-03-25. Customer agreed to token-exchange workaround to speed immediate recovery.
next_steps: ENG: PR for adaptive coalesce logic (assigned to @alan-martin) - target 2026-03-25
SRE: Monitor rollout for next 72 hours and roll back if CPU syscalls > threshold
CS: Follow up with ParcelFlow on token-exchange adoption and collect UX metrics
Postmortem: Drafted and will be published after production validation (owner: Maya Lopez)
